All four reviewers gave positive evaluations (two borderline accepts and two accepts), praising the novelty of the benchmark and the sufficiency of the experimental evaluation. While the reviewers suggested clarifying the description of the dataset and offered several suggestions regarding the experimental evaluation, these issues were well addressed in the rebuttal, and all reviewers maintained their initial ratings. Therefore, the AC recommends acceptance of this paper.

author_final_remarks.value:
We sincerely thank all reviewers for your thoughtful engagement and constructive suggestions.

---
We are encouraged by your consistent recognition of 3EED as a significant and impactful benchmark for unifying multi-platform 3D visual grounding, as well as the clarity, scale, and rigor of our dataset design and the proposed grounding framework.

---
During the discussion phase, we addressed all raised concerns with concrete clarifications and updates:

* **Dataset Design & Coverage** – Clarified the empirical motivation for multi-platform coverage (vehicle, drone, quadruped) and the process for selecting diverse scenes; added statistics for distribution across platforms, cities, and object categories.

* **Annotation Pipeline** – Provided empirical evidence of the efficiency and quality gains from the VLM-assisted annotation pipeline through controlled comparisons with fully manual annotations; described bias mitigation strategies and validation procedures.

* **Benchmark Evaluation** – Reported additional results for frame-only and LiDAR-only baselines; detailed evaluation metrics, per-attribute tracking, and object-level difficulty labels to ensure comprehensive assessment.

* **Methodology** – Elaborated on the framework's multi-modal fusion and expert selection mechanisms; added ablations isolating each modality and expert configuration.

* **Extensions & Generality** – Outlined plans to extend 3EED to additional object classes, scene domains, and multi-object grounding tasks; highlighted compatibility with broader 3D/4D grounding research.

These clarifications reinforce the scientific rigor, scalability, and lasting value of 3EED. By introducing the first large-scale, multi-platform 3D grounding benchmark with a hybrid VLM-human annotation pipeline, the work enables unified evaluation across modalities and domains, while our framework establishes strong baselines for future research.

---
We believe 3EED fills a critical gap in 3D grounding research, providing both a benchmark and methods of enduring utility to the community, and paving the way for advances in unified, cross-platform, multi-modal understanding.

---
Once again, we sincerely thank you for the time and effort you devoted to this review!

*Yours sincerely,*

The Authors of Submission 69

**Dear Reviewers, ACs, and SACs,**

We sincerely thank you all for your valuable time, thoughtful feedback, and constructive suggestions!

---
We are encouraged by the **recognition** of our contributions, including:

* Reviewer `MjDg` recognizes this work as *“significant extension”* and *“multi-platform unification”*.
* Reviewer `uL1B` recognizes this work as *“novel benchmark”* and *“well-organized experiments”*.
* Reviewer `GkTs` recognizes this work as *“first to support multi-platform outdoor grounding”* and *“rich evaluations”*.
* Reviewer `iwxg` recognizes this work as *“high-quality benchmark”* and *“potential for embodied 3D perception”*.

---
In response to your insightful comments, we have made the following **clarifications and improvements**:

- **Annotation Efficiency & Quality**
  - As suggested by Reviewers `MjDg` and `uL1B`, we added a study comparing fully manual and VLM-assisted pipelines, showing \~2× speed-up while maintaining expression quality. Details are in the supplement.

- **Implementation & Experiments**
  - As suggested by Reviewer `MjDg`, we included *WildRefer* \[ECCV’24] and demonstrated our method’s superior performance across all platforms and evaluation settings.
  - As suggested by Reviewer `iwxg`, we highlighted how 3EED captures these challenges and how our CPA, MSS, and SAF modules mitigate them.
  - As suggested by Reviewer `iwxg`, we analyzed performance drops from ground to aerial views and explained how our design addresses viewpoint and sparsity gaps.

- **Dataset Scope & Use Cases**
  - As suggested by Reviewer `GkTs`, we clarified category selection, scalability to more classes, and relevance to downstream tasks like navigation and manipulation.

- **Accessibility**
  - As suggested by Reviewer `iwxg`, we noted that 3EED is <10GB and trainable within 12 hours on a single A100. We also provide a lightweight subset and toolkit.

- **Ethical Considerations**
  - As suggested by Reviewer `iwxg`, we elaborated on privacy protections, environmental efficiency, and responsible usage in our release policy.

---
We would like to re-emphasize the **key contributions** of this work:

- 3EED: the first benchmark for multi-platform 3D visual grounding in real-world outdoor scenes.
- A hybrid VLM-human annotation pipeline for scalable, high-quality expression generation.
- Comprehensive evaluations and new robustness modules (CPA, MSS, SAF) across diverse platforms.

---
With **two days** remaining in the **Author-Reviewer Discussion** phase (*August 6, Anywhere on Earth*), we welcome any further questions or suggestions and remain available to engage.

Thank you once again for your kind support and consideration!

*Warmest regards,*

The Authors of Submission 69

We sincerely thank Reviewer `iwxg` for the thorough and constructive review. We are encouraged that you find 3EED to be a well-organized, high-quality benchmark with diverse real-world coverage, meaningful baseline design, and strong potential for advancing embodied 3D perception. We address your insightful comments below.

---

> **`Q1`:** *"Clarification on the cross-platform performance degradation, especially when transferring from ground-based platforms to aerial views."*

**A:** We fully agree that cross-platform generalization -- particularly from ground (vehicle/quadruped) to aerial (drone) views -- is a significant challenge. Drone data introduces unique difficulties such as **extremely sparse point clouds**, **large viewpoint shifts**, and **increased occlusion**, which together degrade grounding performance.

One of our key motivations in building 3EED was precisely to surface such real-world challenges. To address them, we proposed a suite of adaptations in Section `4.2`:
- **Cross-Platform Alignment (CPA):** Normalizes gravity and object height across platforms.
- **Multi-Scale Sampling (MSS):** Enhances object-level representations across varying sizes.
- **Scale-Aware Fusion (SAF):** Mitigates the effect of point cloud sparsity.

These designs led to substantial improvements, as shown in Table `2`. Nonetheless, performance gaps remain. As reported in Table `6`, drone scenes average only **93.27 points per object** (vs. over 1,400 in vehicle scenes), with an average of **8.57 objects per frame**, making disambiguation especially difficult. 

We believe 3EED provides a valuable testbed to inspire further research into **platform-agnostic**, **scale-aware**, and **sparsity-robust** grounding models.

---

> **`Q2`:** *"Clarification on the dataset’s performance in sparse or high-density scenes, and future directions for enhancing model robustness under such conditions."*

**A:** Thank you for highlighting this important limitation. As shown in Table `5`, sparse or densely populated scenes indeed present serious grounding challenges. These cases are **deliberately included** in 3EED to reveal failure modes under **difficult, real-world conditions**.

To address such cases, we introduced **MSS** and **SAF** modules (Section `4.2`), which yielded notable gains for drone views (Table `2`). Still, this remains an open area. We plan to:
- Incorporate **richer sensing modalities** (e.g., higher-resolution LiDAR, RGB-D cameras).
- Encourage **adaptive training strategies** that account for varying density and occlusion.
- Maintain backward compatibility to ensure benchmark stability.

We hope these efforts will promote robust grounding models that can generalize to both **data-rich** and **data-poor** scenarios.

---

> **`Q3`:** *"Clarification on the computational and storage demands, and steps taken to improve accessibility."*

**A:** We appreciate this point and have taken active steps to minimize resource barriers. Specifically:
- The entire 3EED dataset (RGB, LiDAR, annotations) is **<10GB**, significantly smaller than benchmarks like nuScenes (~100GB+), enabling fast download and storage on standard systems.
- Our baselines can be trained **within 12 hours on a single A100 GPU**, with full cross-platform coverage. We will report exact training times in our revision.
- We also provide a **visualization and querying toolkit** (Supp. Fig. `B`), allowing users to interactively explore expressions, predictions, and scene geometry with minimal setup.

Furthermore, we are preparing a **lightweight subset** of 3EED for quick experimentation and educational use in resource-constrained environments.

---

> **`Q4`:** *"Request for deeper discussion on ethical risks (e.g., surveillance) and environmental impact of large-scale data collection and training."*

**A:** We thank the reviewer for highlighting the importance of ethical and societal considerations. As a publicly released multi-platform visual perception dataset, we fully agree that potential misuse risks and environmental impact should be carefully addressed.

**Misuse Risks & Privacy Protection**  
We have taken proactive steps to mitigate privacy concerns and reduce the potential for misuse, as detailed below:

- All data was collected in public spaces, strictly avoiding any private or indoor environments.  
- Sensitive information, such as faces and license plates, has been automatically blurred and manually verified to ensure no personally identifiable information (PII) remains.  
- Importantly, 3EED does not contain sequential video or temporal tracking annotations, making it infeasible to reconstruct trajectories or perform identity association.

While we believe the current version greatly minimizes privacy exposure, we are also aware of potential misuse scenarios, such as surveillance or behavioral profiling. To mitigate this, we have explicitly prohibited such applications in our dataset license and plan to continuously update our usage policy to promote responsible use within the community.

**Environmental Impact**  
We have also considered the computational and environmental costs of data hosting and model training:

- The full dataset size is under 10GB, significantly lighter than many existing benchmarks (e.g., nuScenes, Waymo).  
- Our baselines are designed to be resource-efficient, requiring less than 24 hours of training on a single A100 GPU for the full dataset.  
- We also host 3EED on the Hugging Face Datasets Hub, which offers cloud-backed, geographically distributed, and streaming-compatible access, helping reduce data redundancy and download overhead across users.

As suggested, we have expanded on these points in our updated documentation and remain committed to supporting sustainable and ethical AI practices in 3D perception and grounding research.

---

Last but not least, we would like to sincerely thank Reviewer `iwxg` again for the valuable time and constructive feedback provided during this review.

We sincerely thank Reviewer `GkTs` for the thoughtful and constructive review. We are encouraged that you recognize 3EED as the first dataset to support multi-platform outdoor 3D visual grounding, and appreciate the thorough evaluations, detailed platform analysis, and data richness in elevation, density, and viewpoint diversity. Below, we respond to your insightful comments.

---

> **`Q1`:** *"Clarification on the dataset’s semantic coverage and its potential limitations in supporting diverse real-world scenarios."*

**A:** We appreciate your concern regarding semantic diversity. The current object categories in 3EED -- such as vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists -- were deliberately chosen due to their **critical importance in real-world robotic applications**, particularly in urban environments. These classes are the **most safety-critical** and **frequently encountered**, making them highly relevant for autonomous driving, navigation, and surveillance systems.

At the same time, we emphasize that 3EED is **not a static dataset**, but a **scalable framework** for large-scale grounding. Our hybrid VLM-assisted annotation pipeline enables efficient extension to additional categories as needed. While the current version focuses on high-priority classes, the pipeline **generalizes well to more object types**, and we plan to broaden coverage in future updates.

Importantly, within each class, we ensured **rich linguistic variation**. Expressions include diverse descriptors for appearance, motion, spatial relations, and contextual cues -- examples of which are showcased in Figures `C` to `F` of the supplementary material. This helps simulate the kind of fine-grained, grounded language understanding required for embodied agents.

We will also release the **pre-annotated 3D bounding boxes (without expressions)**, together with our **VLM-assisted annotation pipeline** and **human verification interface**, to facilitate the expansion to new object categories, support customized expression generation, and encourage broader community contributions.

---

> **`Q2`:** *"Clarification on the relatively modest number of expressions (25k) given the dataset scale."*

**A:** Thank you for raising this point. Although 3EED contains over **134k 3D objects**, we chose to release **25k manually verified referring expressions** to ensure **high annotation quality**. This decision was informed by three key considerations:
1. **Expression precision:** Not every object instance is suitable for generating an unambiguous 3D expression, especially in crowded scenes or under occlusions. We selected only those that passed strict human verification standards to ensure **grounding clarity** and **training utility**.
2. **Annotation cost and human oversight:** Despite the gains from our VLM-assisted pipeline, human verification remains crucial. We therefore prioritized **coverage across all three platforms** and **diverse viewpoints**, rather than fully annotating every instance.
3. **Augmentation and scalability:** We include a **language-level paraphrasing module** to generate diverse variations of each expression, thus expanding training diversity beyond raw count. Our annotation framework is also **scalable** and can support future extensions to grow both expression quantity and object coverage.

---

> **`Q3`:** *"Clarification on how 3EED supports downstream tasks such as navigation or manipulation."*

**A:** We fully agree that one of the core strengths of 3EED lies in its potential utility for **embodied AI tasks**. While the current paper focuses on 3D grounding, the dataset is intentionally designed to serve as a foundation for **language-conditioned embodied perception and action**.

For example:
- In **navigation tasks**, 3D grounding outputs precise coordinates of the referred target, which can serve as goals for a planning or control policy (e.g., *“navigate to the orange cone next to the mailbox”*).
- In **manipulation**, the agent can use the grounded 3D location to approach and interact with the referred object (e.g., grasping or inspection).
- More broadly, 3EED supports the **perception module in instruction-following pipelines**, allowing grounding of language inputs to actionable spatial representations.

In our revision, we have expanded the discussion to highlight these downstream use cases, and articulated how 3EED complements tasks such as VLN, EQA, or open-vocabulary rearrangement.

---

We sincerely thank Reviewer `uL1B` for the positive and detailed review. We are grateful that you recognize 3EED as a novel and impactful benchmark for 3D visual grounding, appreciate the diversity and scale of our dataset, and find the experiments and manuscript presentation to be clear and well-organized. Below, we address your insightful question.

---

> **`Q1`:** *"Clarification on the effort and impact of human verification in the annotation pipeline, and the feasibility of full automation."*

**A:** We appreciate your thoughtful inquiry regarding the design trade-offs in our annotation pipeline. To quantify the effort and efficiency gains, we conducted a study between **fully manual annotation** and our **hybrid VLM-assisted pipeline** (with `Qwen2-VL-72B`). Specifically, we randomly sampled  **100 object instances**, which were annotated by **6 experienced annotators**, and analyzed both efficiency and quality outcomes under two settings:
- For **fully manual** annotation, writing a high-quality 3D referring expression took an average of **55.6 seconds** per retained expression.
- In the **VLM-assisted** setting, each expression takes an average of **~7.2 seconds** to generate via the VLM and **~10.2 seconds** for human verification, refinement, or rejection. Among these, **78 expressions** were ultimately retained. To fairly estimate annotation efficiency, we divide the total time spent across all 100 cases by the number of retained expressions, yielding an effective annotation cost of approximately **~28.6 seconds per accepted expression**.

This demonstrates that our proposed hybrid pipeline achieves **~2x speed-up** compared to the fully manual setting.

In terms of impact on **annotation quality**, our analysis revealed that:
- **31%** of the VLM-generated expressions were accepted **as-is**.
- **47%** required **minor edits** (e.g., refining spatial cues or object attributes).
- **22%** were **discarded** due to being irrelevant to the object.

These findings suggest that human verification plays a crucial role in preserving linguistic precision and spatial clarity, even as model-assisted annotation substantially reduces workload. We have included the details on this study in the revised supplementary file. 

Lastly, regarding the **feasibility of full automation**, our results indicate that current VLMs are not yet reliable enough to handle complex outdoor scenes without supervision. While promising, their outputs still occasionally lack the grounding accuracy needed for high-quality benchmarks. We thus believe that our **hybrid pipeline offers a practical and scalable balance** between automation and quality control, and it lays the groundwork for future research into reducing or eliminating the need for human oversight.

---

Last but not least, we would like to sincerely thank Reviewer `uL1B` again for the valuable time and constructive feedback provided during this review.

summary.value: This work introduce 3EED, a multi-platform, multi-modal 3D grounding benchmark featuring RGB and LiDAR data covering both vehicle-mounted and drone-based platforms, with unify single-object and multi-object 3D  grounding tasks into a large-scale benchmark focused on outdoor environments. The VLM pipeline and human filter are included to provide the annotation.

strengths_contributions.value:
This paper makes a significant extension of existing benchmarks by introducing a dataset that covers both vehicle-mounted and drone-based platforms. The dataset expands the range of scenarios and unifies single-object and multi-object 3D  grounding tasks into a large-scale benchmark focused on outdoor environments. In addition, the authors propose methods specifically tailored to this new setting.

The paper also presents a hybrid annotation pipeline: prompts are first generated by a vision-language model and then verified by human annotators. The authors develop a structured toolchain to generate dense and unambiguous referring expressions for grounding tasks in a more efficient and cost-effective manner.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
Lack of Quantitative Evidence on Annotation Efficiency and Accuracy

Although the paper claims that the vision-language model-assisted workflow significantly improves annotation efficiency, it does not provide empirical evidence to support this claim. For example: How much speed-up does the hybrid annotation method achieve compared to fully manual annotation? What proportion of the model-generated labels require human correction? How is the overall annotation quality ensured while improving efficiency? Without quantitative analysis, it is difficult to assess the real trade-offs among annotation cost, speed, and quality.

Limited Baseline Selection

The dataset primarily focuses on outdoor scenarios. However, the baselines selected in the paper are relatively outdated and mostly designed for indoor settings. In fact, there are several grounding methods specifically developed for outdoor environments. How do these methods perform on the 3EED dataset? Including such methods in the comparison would better demonstrate the challenges posed by the dataset and validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. The dataset focuses primarily on vehicles and pedestrians, which may limit its usefulness for grounding more semantically diverse real-world scenarios
2. While the object count is impressive, the 25k expressions seem modest given the scale of the dataset and the goal of modeling fine-grained, language-conditioned perception.
3. The dataset is designed for embodied agents, yet the paper does not demonstrate how 3EED can benefit downstream tasks like instruction-following, navigation or manipulation.

summary.value:
This paper presents 3EED, a large-scale, multi-platform, multi-modal benchmark for 3D visual grounding in outdoor environments. 3EED distinguishes itself by providing synchronized LiDAR and RGB data from three robotic platforms: vehicles, drones, and quadrupeds. The dataset includes over 134,000 annotated 3D objects and more than 25,000 human-verified referring expressions, making it larger than previous outdoor 3D grounding datasets. The authors introduce a scalable annotation pipeline that combines vision-language model prompting with human validation and propose platform-aware normalization and cross-modal alignment techniques. 
Extensive benchmark protocols and baseline evaluations are established to support in-domain and cross-platform research. The 3EED dataset and toolkit are made publicly available to foster further research in language-driven embodied 3D perception.

strengths_contributions.value:
1. The dataset is substantially larger than previous outdoor datasets (Table 1), with diverse outdoor scenes and fine-grained human-verified language supervision. The platform diversity and large-scale coverage ensure 3EED is highly relevant for real-world, cross-platform deployment scenarios.

2. The paper introduces platform-aware normalization and cross-modal alignment methods, as well as a strong, scale-adaptive, agent-invariant baseline. These are shown to meaningfully improve cross-platform transfer and robustness, with extensive experimental results and ablation studies (see Tables 2–6, Figures 4–6)

3. The paper is well-organized, clearly written, and includes informative figures, tables, and detailed appendix material. The dataset and code are made available on reputable public platforms.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. As noted in the results (Tables 2–6), SOTA models, including the authors’ strong baseline, still exhibit substantial performance drops when transferred across platforms, especially from ground (vehicle/quadruped) to aerial (drone) data. While this demonstrates the value of the benchmark, it also highlights the difficulty of the problem and the need for further model innovation.

2. Performance is particularly poor in scenarios with sparse point clouds (e.g., drone views) and scenes with high object density (Table 5). The dataset could be further enhanced by including more diverse sensors or by providing additional guidance for model adaptation to these extreme conditions.

3. The large scale and multi-modal nature of the dataset imply significant computational and storage demands. Although this is typical for high-impact benchmarks, it may restrict usage by some in the community. Providing more lightweight data versions or toolkits for efficient data handling could broaden accessibility.

4. While the paper addresses some ethical and societal impacts in the appendix, a deeper discussion regarding the potential for misuse (e.g., surveillance) and the environmental impact of large-scale data collection and model training would further strengthen the ethical evaluation.

ethical_considerations.value: No, there are no or only very minor ethics concerns

ethical_comments.value: While the societal impact of 3D perception technologies can include potential concerns such as surveillance or bias, the authors’ open discussion in the appendix is sufficient for this stage. I recommend that the authors continue to monitor these considerations as the dataset gains broader adoption.

dataset_code_comments.value: The dataset and code are both publicly accessible, hosted on Hugging Face and GitHub.

1. Including more discussion and guidelines for responsible downstream use (especially in sensitive applications) would be beneficial.

abstract.value: Visual grounding in 3D is the key for embodied agents to localize language-referred objects in open-world environments. However, existing benchmarks are limited to indoor focus, single-platform constraints, and small scale. We introduce 3EED, a multi-platform, multi-modal 3D grounding benchmark featuring RGB and LiDAR data from vehicle, drone, and quadruped platforms. We provide over 128,000 objects and 22,000 validated referring expressions across diverse outdoor scenes -- 10x larger than existing datasets. We develop a scalable annotation pipeline combining vision-language model prompting with human verification to ensure high-quality spatial grounding. To support cross-platform learning, we propose platform-aware normalization and cross-modal alignment techniques, and establish benchmark protocols for in-domain and cross-platform evaluations. Our findings reveal significant performance gaps, highlighting the challenges and opportunities of generalizable 3D grounding. The 3EED dataset and benchmark toolkit are released to advance future research in language-driven 3D embodied perception.

dataset_URL.description: If you checked the Dataset Submission box, provide the URL to your dataset here. **Before including the URL for your dataset, verify that you followed the [NeurIPS2025 data hosting guidelines](https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/DataHostingGuidelines) (as part of the CFPs) and that the URL is accessible to NeurIPS2025 reviewers.** If you left the Dataset Submission box unchecked, leave this field empty.

dataset_final_confirmation.description: **By checking this box, you confirm that: (1)** your dataset is complete and finalized at the time of submission; **(2)** you included a valid Croissant metadata file that has been verified using the [Croissant validator](https://huggingface.co/spaces/luisoala/croissant-checker); **(3)** you followed the [NeurIPS2025 data hosting guidelines](https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/DataHostingGuidelines); **(4)** you provided a URL pointing to the dataset that is accessible for NeurIPS2025 reviewers. If you left the Dataset Submission box unchecked, leave this box unchecked.

code_URL.description: If your submission includes code, provide the URL to a hosting platform (e.g., Github, Bitbucket) as described in the CFPs. See the main track [code guidelines](https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy) for details.

supplementary_material.description: All supplementary material must be self-contained and zipped into a single file. Note that supplementary material will be visible to reviewers throughout and after the review period, and **ensure all your supplementary material is anonymized if your submission is anonymized.** The maximum file size is 100MB. Supplementary material can be updated until the supplementary material deadline (May 22).

financial_support.description: Optionally indicate one student author on the paper who would need financial support to attend and present at the conference if the paper is accepted (or leave blank if financial support is not needed). Please enter an email address or an OpenReview ID that exactly matches one of the authors.

reviewer_nomination.description: Every submission must nominate at least one author who is a qualified reviewer (i.e., satisfying our reviewer nomination criteria [https://blog.neurips.cc/2025/03/10/self-nomination-for-reviewing-at-neurips-2025/](https://blog.neurips.cc/2025/03/10/self-nomination-for-reviewing-at-neurips-2025/) ). Being named as such a reviewer in the submission constitutes an acceptance and a commitment to carry out the regular reviewing load (~6 papers) responsibly if asked by the PC chairs or the D&B track chairs. Only if no qualified reviewer exists in the author list, nominate the best-qualified author for consideration by the PC chairs or the D&B track chairs. In addition, note that any author listed on 4 or more papers will be automatically regarded as a reviewer unless they are already serving as a reviewer, AC, SAC, or other roles in the Organization Committee. Failure to assign a qualified reviewer when one is available in the author list may result in desk rejection. Please enter an email address or an OpenReview ID that exactly matches one of the authors (separate by comma if more than one nominations).

responsible_reviewing.description: We acknowledge that every author on the program committee is obligated to conduct responsible reviewing according to the policy designed by the PC Chairs and relevant members of the organizing committee. **Failure to do so may result in desk rejection or other serious consequences.**
